# `x4effective`

```text
usage: x4effective [-h] [--version] [--db DB]
                   {build,ls,show,attr,who-sets,diff-mod,dump,sql,coverage,find,card} ...

Browse the effective merged values of every X4 entity, with provenance.

positional arguments:
  {build,ls,show,attr,who-sets,diff-mod,dump,sql,coverage,find,card}
    build               (re)build the effective store
    ls                  list entities of a kind
    show                all props + provenance for one entity
    attr                one prop across all entities of a class
    who-sets            provenance chain for an entity['s prop]
    diff-mod            every value a mod wins
    dump                live effective XML for ANY vpath (incl. md/, aiscripts/)
    sql                 read-only SELECT against the store
    coverage            what this store DOES and does not index (so a negative can carry its
                        denominator)
    find                entities whose in-game NAME contains TEXT (resolves {page,id} to English);
                        exit 0 a match, 1 none among the names searched, 3 nothing to search
    card                one macro's identity: in-game name and description, weapon system, what it
                        fires, fitting tags and size, ware and price, and which loadouts.xml
                        entries and ship macros name it (loadoutrules are not indexed), each value
                        with the source that set it; exit 0 card printed, 1 no such macro

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --db DB               effective store to read or build (default: $X4_EFFECTIVE_DB, or derived
                        from $X4_MODS / $X4_REGISTRY)
```

## `x4effective build`

```text
usage: x4effective build [-h] [--reference REFERENCE] [--kinds KINDS]

  --reference REFERENCE
                        unpacked base+DLC tree to build from (default: the configured reference
                        tree)
  --kinds KINDS         comma-separated entity kinds to build (default: ware,job,ship,shipgroup,lo
                        adout,station,stationgroup,module,modulegroup,plan,basket,people,mapdatase
                        t,sound,icon,gfxeffect,roomgroup,room,character,region,faction,macro,compo
                        nent)
```

## `x4effective ls`

```text
usage: x4effective ls [-h] [--class KLASS] [--filter FILTER] [--modified-only] [--limit LIMIT]
                      kind

positional arguments:
  kind             entity kind as stored, e.g. ware, macro, job

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --class KLASS    only entities of this class (the store's class column)
  --filter FILTER  substring match on name
  --modified-only  only entities a MOD changed -- the entity, any of its attributes, or a removal
                   in its own file; base/DLC-only rows are hidden
  --limit LIMIT    rows to print; the total is still counted (default: 200)
```

## `x4effective attr`

```text
usage: x4effective attr [-h] [--class KLASS] [--sort {num,name}] [--limit LIMIT] kind prop

positional arguments:
  kind               entity kind as stored, e.g. ware, macro, job
  prop               property key as the store spells it, e.g. hull.max (macro keys carry no
                     properties. prefix)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --class KLASS      only entities of this class (the store's class column)
  --sort {num,name}  order by numeric value or by entity name (default: name)
  --limit LIMIT      rows to print; the total is still counted (default: 200)
```

## `x4effective dump`

```text
usage: x4effective dump [-h] [--reference REFERENCE] [--chain] [--annotate] vpath

positional arguments:
  vpath                 path inside the game tree, e.g. libraries/wares.xml

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --reference REFERENCE
                        unpacked base+DLC tree to build from (default: the configured reference
                        tree)
  --chain               also print the file-level source chain
  --annotate            mark every node an overlay changed with a comment naming the mod, op and
                        patch line (removals listed in a header); implies --chain. Records who WON
                        each node, not who introduced it (F64); after a whole-file replace no node
                        is annotated and the header names the replacing mod; no attribute history
                        is kept inside a replaced subtree (F338)
```

## `x4effective sql`

```text
usage: x4effective sql [-h] [--json] query

Run one read-only query. Default output is TSV: cells are TAB-separated, one row per line; inside
a cell a backslash prints as \\, a TAB as \t, a newline as \n, a carriage return as \r, and SQL
NULL as \N (an empty string stays empty). --json prints the exact values instead.

positional arguments:
  query       one read-only SELECT or WITH statement (anything else is refused)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print {schema, columns, rows} as one JSON object, values exact and NULL as null
              (default: escaped TSV, no header row)
```

## `x4effective card`

```text
usage: x4effective card [-h] [--json] [--limit LIMIT] macro

Print the facts that classify one macro (a weapon, turret, missile, shield, engine, or any other),
each value with the source that WON it: a mod, or 'no override, still vanilla' (base or a DLC). A
field is resolved, ABSENT (the store holds the entity and it has no such value) or NOT RESOLVED (a
reference the store cannot follow), never blank. Text prints as one quoted JSON string literal per
line; a t-file that writes a literal backslash-n shows it as \\n, not as a line break. Carriers
are literal mentions in libraries/loadouts.xml and ship macros only: loadoutrules, which fit most
NPC ships, are not indexed, so none found is NOT RESOLVED. For a missile launcher or missile
turret, 'fires' is only the default bullet; the ammunition tags decide what it loads. --json
carries the store's freshness verdict. Exit 0 the card was printed (a field may still be NOT
RESOLVED), 1 no macro of that name is in the store, 2 the store is unreadable.

positional arguments:
  macro          the macro's name (its id), e.g. turret_arg_m_flak_01_mk1_macro; a ware id is
                 pointed at its macro

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --json         print the card as one JSON object, schema x4effective.card/1, every carrier
                 included (default: text)
  --limit LIMIT  carriers to print in the text form; the total is still counted, 0 for all
                 (default: 20)
```
